verdicts.claim: SQLite provides five checkpoint modes: PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART, TRUNCATE, and NOOP. PASSIVE is the default mode used by automatic
verdicts.evidence: c3ref lists all five modes; wal.html: 'All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.'

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL mode blocks until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent snapshot
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'This mode blocks ... until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.'

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART works like FULL with the addition that it blocks until all readers are reading from the database file
verdicts.evidence: c3ref RESTART text matches near-verbatim, incl. 'next writer will restart the log file from the beginning'.

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE works the same as RESTART but also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to successful return
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.'

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP always checkpoints zero frames; its purpose is solely to access status information via output parameters
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned ... via output parameters'. (zylos does not mention NOOP.)

verdicts.claim: Automatic WAL checkpointing triggers when the WAL file reaches 1000 pages (approximately 4MB at default 4KB page size), modifiable via wal_autocheckpoint
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'accumulates about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB in size)'; threshold changeable via wal_autocheckpoint pragma.

verdicts.claim: FULL and RESTART checkpoints can only be initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() function calls, while automatic checkpoints and sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() use PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §3.2: 'FULL and RESTART checkpoints ... can only be initiated by a call to sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2().'

verdicts.claim: rqlite, a distributed SQLite system, explicitly disables automatic checkpointing and manages checkpoints manually
verdicts.evidence: O'Toole: rqlite disables auto-checkpointing and 'issues explicit checkpoints as part of the snapshotting process'. Zylos does not mention rqlite, so the '(two sources)' tag is overstated.

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint starvation occurs when a concurrent reader prevents the checkpoint from resetting the WAL file ... unbounded WAL growth
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §6: 'the checkpoint cannot reset the WAL file because doing so might delete content out from under the reader ... the WAL file will grow without bound.' (c1-3 fetch returned 503.)

verdicts.claim: Busy timeout does not apply to checkpoint operations—if busy_timeout is 0, the checkpoint call returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately when blocked by
verdicts.evidence: Zylos claims 'The timeout is ignored for checkpoint operations' (forum c1-5 says nothing on it), but primary c3ref/wal_checkpoint_v2: 'The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes ... a busy-handler is configured, it is invoked ... The busy-handler is also invoked while waiting for database readers.'

notes: Overview says 'SQLite provides four checkpoint modes' while Core Concepts says five (incl. NOOP); internal inconsistency.
The '(two sources)' tags are overstated for the rqlite claim (zylos never mentions rqlite) and the busy-timeout claim (the forum thread never discusses busy_timeout).
